findings.title: PR comment workflow calls helpers on the wrong object
findings.body: `self` here is a `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`, but `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` was added to `CommitContextIntegration`, so generating a merged-PR comment raises `AttributeError`. The equivalent GitLab workflow makes the same call. Moreover, the helper itself calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, although `_truncate_title` was also added to `CommitContextIntegration`; fixing only the call site would still leave comment generation failing.

findings.title: Feature-enabled dashboard tables are rendered with empty data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch passes `columns: []` and an empty `tableData` instead of the current `result` data and fields. The new visualization therefore renders a blank table for every dashboard table widget using the feature, even when the query returned rows.

findings.title: Error and breadcrumb timestamps use different units
findings.body: This compares an issue event's nodestore timestamp (Unix seconds) directly with the raw replay recording event timestamp (RRWeb milliseconds). In real replays, the comparison treats errors as occurring before breadcrumbs, so the combined log sent for summarization is chronologically incorrect. Convert both timestamps to the same unit before comparing; the added test misses this because it supplies breadcrumb timestamps in seconds.

findings.title: Reports with no age or timestamp are accepted
findings.body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, and the cross-field validators only run when their respective fields are supplied. Consequently, a report containing neither field passes validation; when both are zero, the truthiness checks also fail to reject the mutually exclusive pair. Malformed reports are then counted as valid received reports. Validate field presence explicitly and require exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes remain visible when the search is empty
findings.body: The empty-search branch returns `sorted` before applying `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES`; the new exclusion runs only when a search term is entered. As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are shown in the normal attributes view despite being designated as hidden.

findings.title: Falsey custom cell output incorrectly falls back to the default renderer
findings.body: The custom-renderer contract says fallback occurs when the callback returns `undefined`, but this truthiness check also falls back for valid outputs such as `null`, `0`, or an empty string. A renderer therefore cannot intentionally leave a cell blank or render a numeric zero. The head-cell renderer has the same truthiness check at line 31.
